title: LMCache/LMCache Release v0.5.3rc4 · CUDA 12.9
problem: Deploying LMCache with CUDA-based vLLM stacks requires a package compatible with CUDA 12.9 and a resolver configuration that can select the matching PyTorch wheel without pulling incompatible builds.
mechanism: The release publishes a CUDA 12.9 wheel for LMCache v0.5.3rc4 and documents installation with uv pip, PyTorch's cu129 extra index, the GitHub expanded-assets wheel directory, and unsafe-best-match index strategy.

evidence.claim: LMCache v0.5.3rc4 has a CUDA 12.9 wheel.
The documented install uses uv pip with the PyTorch cu129 extra index and LMCache expanded-assets link.

evaluation_context: This is an official LMCache GitHub packaging release for CUDA 12.9. It provides a wheel and resolver command but no KV-cache throughput, network latency, model-serving, or compatibility matrix beyond the CUDA target.
limitations: The release candidate note does not report performance or prove compatibility with every PyTorch, vLLM, driver, or GPU combination using CUDA 12.9. The documented unsafe-best-match resolver strategy can select packages from multiple indexes and should be validated in a locked environment. The page includes GitHub loading-error placeholders around the short release body.
project_relevance: This is an integration prerequisite for reproducing LMCache/KV-cache transfer experiments on CUDA 12.9, not evidence that LMCache improves TPN scheduling, transfer volume, or end-to-end token latency. Record the exact CUDA/PyTorch/vLLM environment before comparing network results (inference).
source_notes: Facts extracted from the fetched official LMCache GitHub release page; title copied exactly from input metadata.
No performance claims were inferred from the packaging release.
